causebase_summary: Alcoholics Anonymous, Perth, Western Australia (Aa Service Council For Western Australia) is a local fellowship supporting people who identify a desire to stop drinking. It maintains a staffed office in East Perth with published opening hours (Monday–Friday, 9am–4.30pm) and operates a 24‑hour helpline. The group compiles and publishes meeting lists and a calendar of events (including open and online meetings), provides resources for new members (pamphlets, personal stories, talks and workshops), and publishes or links to AA literature and Serenity magazine. The organisation also maintains a safety policy, code of conduct and incident reporting forms. Open meetings are available to anyone interested in AA’s programme of recovery; the site includes specific contact options for fly‑in/fly‑out workers.

data.SummaryOfActivities: We provide membership services to Alcoholics Anonymous and support people struggling with alcohol to get to an AA meeting and to get sober.   Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of people who share their experience, strength and hope with each other that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism.  The only requirement for membership is a desire to stop drinking. There are no dues or fees for A.A. membership; we are self-supporting through our own contributions.  A.A. is not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organisation or institution; does not wish to engage in any controversy; neither endorses nor opposes any causes. Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.
